about.title: Goleta Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Goleta residents rely on a mix of local clinics and nearby Santa Barbara County hospitals for everything from routine care to surgery, and most visits go fine. But when a provider misses a diagnosis, makes a surgical error, or mishandles medication, the consequences can follow a patient for years. California's MICRA law sets specific rules for these cases, including short notice windows and a requirement for qualified medical expert review, which makes early guidance important. LawProactive doesn't practice law or represent clients directly; instead, we connect Goleta residents who believe they were harmed by substandard medical care with an independent attorney who can review records, consult medical experts, and explain whether a claim may be viable. There's no cost to get connected, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there's a recovery. A bad outcome by itself isn't proof of malpractice, but if something feels wrong about the care you received, a conversation with an attorney can help you understand your options.

whyChoose.title: Why Goleta Patients Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines Are Shorter Than You'd Expect
items.desc: California generally gives one year from when you discover the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, plus a required 90-day notice before filing suit. Missing these windows can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: Expert Review Is Built Into the Process
items.desc: California law almost always requires a qualified medical expert to support a malpractice claim, so an attorney can help arrange the right medical evaluation before proceeding.

items.title: Understanding the Non-Economic Damages Cap
items.desc: MICRA sets a cap on non-economic damages that adjusts upward each year, and an independent attorney can walk you through how that cap may apply to your specific situation.

items.question: I had a poor outcome after treatment near Hollister Avenue in Goleta — is that automatically malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law recognizes that medicine involves risk, and a bad outcome alone doesn't establish malpractice. What matters is whether the provider's care fell below the accepted standard, which is typically assessed with input from a qualified medical expert.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discovered or reasonably should have discovered the injury, but no more than three years from the date it occurred. There's also a required 90-day notice period before a lawsuit can be filed, so earlier review matters.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No, connecting with an attorney through LawProactive is free. Attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.
